- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly bearish (≤0.33) in recent days, model tends to underestimate prices; increase forecast slightly to avoid underreaction.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots in the next few days; apply a downward correction of 2–5% for the following 3–5 days.
- Model consistently underestimates prices during prolonged bearish sentiment (e.g., 3+ consecutive 0.00 sentiment values); add a 1–3% upward bias to forecast.
- For 30-day forecasts, model shows persistent lag in capturing short-term sentiment shifts; adjust by adding 0.5–1.5% to forecast if sentiment turns bullish within 5 days.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture volatility; increase forecast variance by ±1–2% to reflect uncertainty.
- If recent history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive price drops), model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid overbought conditions.
